messages.content: Predict a human participant’s investment amount in this economic trust game. You are the investor. For each separate partner you start with 1 euro and must choose exactly 0 or 1 euro to send; no other amount is allowed. You keep the amount not sent. The sent amount is multiplied by four for the trustee. If you send 1 euro, the trustee may keep all 4 euros, giving you 0 euros from the round, or return half, so each of you receives 2 euros. If you send 0 euros, you keep 1 euro and the trustee receives 0 euros. You were told that the other players had previously recorded what they would do if sent 1 euro. Your participation payment is 1 euro, and you were told that one randomly selected round would determine an additional payment and the matched player’s payment. You are not shown the current trustee’s response before choosing. Output only the original amount sent in euros, exactly 0 or 1, with no explanation.

Before the game, you were asked your age and gender. An attention check asked how much you liked the sun, but instructed you to select “Other” and write “I have carefully read” instead of using the rating scale. Your personal demographic responses are not supplied in this record. You are an Italian participant. You have made separate investment decisions about partners from the 28 European Union member states included in this study, without trustee-return feedback. After those 28 choices, you answered two rating questions about each of these national groups: Austria, Belgium, Bulgaria, Croatia, Cyprus, Czech Republic, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, France, Germany, Greece, Hungary, Ireland, Italy, Latvia, Lithuania, Luxembourg, Malta, Netherlands, Poland, Portugal, Romania, Slovenia, Spain, Slovakia, Sweden, United Kingdom. The first asked how “warm” (friendly, likeable) they were on average. The second used the original wording “cold” (competent, rational and dominant). Both used a 16-point scale from “not at all” to “very much”. You then indicated agreement with the following statements on a seven-point scale: 1 = Totally disagree, 2 = Quite disagree, 3 = Disagree more than agree, 4 = Neither agree nor disagree, 5 = Agree more than disagree, 6 = Quite agree, 7 = Totally agree.
1. Our country can emerge from its crisis only by returning to its traditional values, giving power to a strong leader and silencing those who spread wrong ideas.
2. Our country desperately needs an energetic leader who will sweep away the immoral ways of life that threaten to ruin it.
3. The increase in sexual offences and other crimes shows that immoral behaviour must be suppressed more harshly if we want to save our social order.
4. Our country can be saved only if we eliminate the corruption that is eroding our moral fibre and traditional values.
5. The situation in our country is becoming so worrying that only forceful measures can put it back on the right path.
6. There is absolutely nothing wrong with the existence of nudist camps.
7. Our country really needs free thinkers who have the courage to challenge traditions, even if this may upset many people.
8. Rather than giving the government the power to impose censorship, it is better to allow obscene or subversive publications to circulate.
9. Gay men and lesbians are as healthy and moral as heterosexuals.
10. It is very positive that young people today have the freedom to protest against what they disagree with and to make their own rules of behaviour.
